reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No direct target engagement data for B7-H3 is reported. However, PSA biomarker responses (45.8% response rate at 2.0 mg, 38.0% at 2.7 mg, with mean PSA changes of -28.7% and -33.1% respectively) suggest some biological activity, though PSA is not a direct measure of B7-H3 engagement. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The PSA responses indicate downstream biological activity consistent with anti-tumor effects, suggesting the antibody-drug conjugate mechanism may be functioning to some degree. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Mixed results across arms and endpoints. Part 1 showed successful 6-month rPFS in both dose arms (69% and 70% vs 47% control), with the higher dose arm achieving successful ORR (30.6%). However, Part 2 showed complete failure with 0% ORR. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Significant cardiac toxicities were observed, particularly at the higher dose (5.8% pericardial effusion, 4.7% atrial fibrillation, 2.3% cardiac arrest in 2.7 mg arm), which may have limited dosing optimization. The trial was terminated for business reasons rather than safety or efficacy concerns.
